***

```{r setup, include=FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(cowplot)
library(DT)
library(gt)

split_param <- function(x) strsplit(x, ",")[[1]]

ziffra_tbl_file       <- params$ziffra_tbl
internal_enrich_files <- split_param(params$internal_enrich)
internal_pi1_files    <- split_param(params$internal_pi1)
jang_enrich_files     <- split_param(params$jang_enrich)
jang_pi1_files        <- split_param(params$jang_pi1)
beta_correlation_file <- params$beta_correlation
cell_types            <- split_param(params$cell_types)   # config cell_types, no pseudotime
cell_types_L1         <- split_param(params$fetal_l1)     # qtl_rep.fetal_l1_types
jang_l1               <- split_param(params$jang_l1)      # qtl_rep.report.jang_l1_order

exp_pcs <- split_param(params$exp_pcs)
exp_pc_map <- setNames(as.integer(sub(".*=", "", exp_pcs)), sub("=.*", "", exp_pcs))

benchmark_pairs <- split_param(params$benchmarks)
benchmark_files <- tibble(rule = sub("=.*", "", benchmark_pairs),
                          file = sub("^[^=]*=", "", benchmark_pairs))

# Pick the one file in a list whose name starts with a given prefix
# (e.g. "GABA_vs_MG_"); files are passed by the rule, so this never globs
pick_file <- function(files, prefix) {
  hit <- files[startsWith(basename(files), prefix)]
  if (length(hit) != 1) stop("Expected one file starting '", prefix, "', found ", length(hit))
  hit
}

gene_lookup <- read_tsv(params$gene_lookup, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(ensembl_gene_id, external_gene_name) |>
  distinct(ensembl_gene_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Smaller-font DT wrapper for wide tables (Opposite effects)
small_dt <- function(df, page_length = 20) {
  datatable(
    df, filter = "top", rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover",
    options = list(
      pageLength = page_length, scrollX = TRUE,
      initComplete = DT::JS(
        "function(settings, json) {",
        "$(this.api().table().container()).css({'font-size': '75%'});",
        "}"
      )
    )
  )
}
```

```{r load-beta-correlation, include=FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
beta_correlation <- read_rds(beta_correlation_file)

paired_betas     <- beta_correlation$paired_betas
opposite_effects <- beta_correlation$opposite_effects
celltype_map     <- beta_correlation$celltype_map

# Add gene symbols (paired_betas/opposite_effects only carry ENSG in `gene`)
paired_betas <- paired_betas |>
  left_join(gene_lookup, by = c("gene" = "ensembl_gene_id"))

opposite_effects <- opposite_effects |>
  left_join(gene_lookup, by = c("gene" = "ensembl_gene_id"))

# Scatter grid colours: grey (not sig. in both), blue (sig. in both, concordant),
# red (sig. in both, discordant). significant_jang is the two-check flag (gene's
# Jang lead SNP AND qval < 0.05).
paired_betas <- paired_betas |>
  mutate(
    concordant = sign(beta_my) == sign(beta_jang),
    point_category = case_when(
      significant_jang & concordant  ~ "concordant_both_sig",
      significant_jang & !concordant ~ "discordant_both_sig",
      TRUE                            ~ "other"
    )
  )

# Per-comparison Pearson r
beta_cor_summary <- paired_betas |>
  group_by(my_cell_type, jang_cell_type) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    r = cor(beta_my, beta_jang, use = "complete.obs"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(comparison = paste(my_cell_type, "vs", jang_cell_type))

comparison_levels <- paste(celltype_map$my_cell, "vs", celltype_map$jang_cell)

# One row per comparison: sig. in fetal & present in adult; also sig. in Jang;
# of those, concordant; of those, discordant
significance_counts <- paired_betas |>
  group_by(my_cell_type, jang_cell_type) |>
  summarise(
    n_fetal_sig_present_adult = n(),
    n_also_sig_jang = sum(significant_jang, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_both_sig_concordant = sum(significant_jang & concordant, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_both_sig_discordant = sum(significant_jang & !concordant, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(comparison = paste(my_cell_type, "vs", jang_cell_type)) |>
  arrange(factor(comparison, levels = comparison_levels))
```

## eQTL replication pipeline steps {.tabset}

***

Replication of our sc-eQTL in snATAC-seq open chromatin regions (OCRs) of the
prenatal human cortex ([Ziffra et al. (2021), PMID:34616060](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34616060/)),
between our level 1 cell types, and in adult brain sn-eQTL from the SingleBrain
meta-analysis (Jang et al. 2026). pi1 is estimated with qvalue
([Storey & Tibshirani (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1530509100)).

***

1. `dwnld_ziffra`: Download Ziffra 2021 snATAC-seq peaks file
2. `snp_lookup`: Get hg38 coordinates of sig. eQTL with biomaRt
3. `atac_enrich`: Test for sig. eQTL enrichment in Ziffra snATAC-seq peaks (block bootstrap)
4. `ziffra_summary`: Combine Ziffra enrichments across cell types (Fig 2E)
5. `cat_nom_qtl`: Combine per-chr nominal eQTL parquet files for pi1
6. `pi1_enrich_internal`: pi1 between our level 1 cell types (Fig 3C)
7. `pi1_enrich_jang`: pi1 between our level 1 cell types and Jang et al. 2026 level 1 cell types (Fig 3D)
8. `beta_correlation`: Fetal vs adult (Jang) eQTL effect-size concordance (Fig 3F)
9. `pi1_enrichment_report`: Generate this report

***

Test direction:

+ Forward: pi1 of our sig. sn-eQTL in the reference nominal eQTL data
+ Reverse: pi1 of the reference sig. eQTL in our nominal sn-eQTL data

+ NA in pi1 test means either:
  + too few overlapping eQTLs (<50) for pi1 calculation
  + pi1 smoother (and bootstrap backup test) failed (also due to few overlaps)

***

### Ziffra {.tabset}

***

#### Primary

***

```{r, ziffra_enrichments, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
combined_data <- read_tsv(ziffra_tbl_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

combined_data %>%
  mutate(
    p_value = signif(p_value, 3),
    mean_permuted_overlap = round(mean_permuted_overlap, 1),
    fold_enrichment = round(fold_enrichment, 2),
    peak_cell_type = str_remove(peak_cell_type, '_MACSpeaks')
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-source_cell_type) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 1. Primary sc-eQTL Enrichment in Ziffra et. al. (2021) snATAC-seq OCRs",
    subtitle = "Observed vs Permuted Overlap"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    eqtl_cell_type = "eQTL Cell Type",
    peak_cell_type = "Peak Cell Type",
    p_value = "P Value",
    observed_overlap = "Observed Overlap",
    mean_permuted_overlap = "Mean Permuted Overlap",
    fold_enrichment = "Fold Enrichment"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(p_value, fold_enrichment),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(mean_permuted_overlap),
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.names = "Arial",
    table.font.size = 12,
    data_row.padding = px(3)
  ) %>%
  opt_table_font(
    font = list(default_fonts())
  )
```

### Internal {.tabset}

***

#### Table

***

```{r, Internal_enrichments, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
read_enrich_tbl <- function(ct, ref_ct) {
  read_rds(pick_file(internal_enrich_files, paste0(ct, "_vs_", ref_ct, "_"))) %>%
    mutate(cell_type = ct,
           ref_cell_type = ref_ct)
}

# Generate all combinations
combinations <- expand.grid(cell_type = cell_types_L1, ref_cell_type = cell_types_L1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Read all enrich tables
pi1_enrich_tbl <- map2_dfr(combinations$cell_type, combinations$ref_cell_type, read_enrich_tbl)
pi1_enrich_tbl %>%
  mutate(
    pi1_cell_ref = ifelse(is.na(pi1_cell_ref), NA, round(as.numeric(pi1_cell_ref), 2)),
    prop_replicating_cell_ref = ifelse(is.na(prop_replicating_cell_ref), NA, round(as.numeric(prop_replicating_cell_ref), 2)),
    prop_same_direction_cell_ref = ifelse(is.na(prop_same_direction_cell_ref), NA, round(as.numeric(prop_same_direction_cell_ref), 2)),
    pi1 = ifelse(is.na(pi1), NA, round(as.numeric(pi1), 2)),
    prop_replicating = ifelse(is.na(prop_replicating), NA, round(as.numeric(prop_replicating), 2)),
    prop_same_direction = ifelse(is.na(prop_same_direction), NA, round(as.numeric(prop_same_direction), 2))
  ) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 5. Internal Pi1 Enrichment Summary cell-specific eQTL"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    cell_type = "Cell Type",
    ref_cell_type = "Reference Cell Type",
    pi1 = "pi1",
    prop_replicating = "Prop. Replicating",
    prop_same_direction = "Prop. Same Dir.",
    overlap_count = "Overlap Count",
    pi1_cell_ref = "pi1",
    prop_replicating_cell_ref = "Prop. Replicating",
    prop_same_direction_cell_ref = "Prop. Same Dir.",
    overlap_count_cell_ref = "Overlap Count"
  ) %>%
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Forward Test",
    columns = c(pi1, prop_replicating, prop_same_direction, overlap_count)
  ) %>%
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Reference Test",
    columns = c(pi1_cell_ref, prop_replicating_cell_ref, prop_same_direction_cell_ref, overlap_count_cell_ref)
  ) %>%
  fmt_missing(
    columns = everything(),
    missing_text = "NA"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = 12,
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
    table.border.top.width = px(2),
    table.border.bottom.width = px(2),
    column_labels.border.top.width = px(2),
    column_labels.border.top.color = "black",
    column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(2),
    column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black"
  )
```

#### Heatmap

***

```{r, internal_heatmap, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.dim=c(6,6)}
# Heatmap order: level 1 cell types in config cell_types order
heatmap_order <- cell_types[cell_types %in% cell_types_L1]

read_pi1_results <- function(ct, ref_ct) {
  pi1_list <- read_rds(pick_file(internal_pi1_files, paste0(ct, "_vs_", ref_ct, "_")))

  tibble(
    cell_type = ct,
    ref_cell_type = ref_ct,
    pi1_forward = pi1_list$forward$pi1,
    pi1_reverse = pi1_list$reverse$pi1,
    prop_replicating_forward = pi1_list$forward$prop_replicating,
    prop_replicating_reverse = pi1_list$reverse$prop_replicating,
    prop_same_direction_forward = pi1_list$forward$prop_same_direction,
    prop_same_direction_reverse = pi1_list$reverse$prop_same_direction
  )
}

# Generate all combinations
combinations <- expand.grid(cell_type = heatmap_order, ref_cell_type = heatmap_order, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Read all pi1 results
pi1_result_tbl <- map2_dfr(combinations$cell_type, combinations$ref_cell_type, read_pi1_results)

# Full 7x7 square of forward pi1 (discovery -> replication is not symmetric);
# diagonal set to 1. Same layout as Fig 3C (manuscript_plot_replication.R),
# without the Glu-A/Glu-B relabelling.
pi1_int_tbl <- pi1_result_tbl %>%
  mutate(pi1_final = ifelse(cell_type == ref_cell_type, 1.0, pi1_forward)) %>%
  select(ref = cell_type, query = ref_cell_type, pi1 = pi1_final) %>%
  mutate(
    # Axis orders as in Fig 3C: replication axis reversed, so the diagonal
    # runs from top-left (MG) to bottom-right (Glu-UL)
    query = factor(query, levels = rev(heatmap_order)),
    ref = factor(ref, levels = heatmap_order)
  )

plot_int_heatmap <- function(df) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = query, y = ref, fill = pi1)) +
    geom_tile(color = "black", lwd = 1.1, linetype = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(pi1), "NA", sprintf("%.2f", pi1))),
              color = "black", size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = c("white", "yellow", "red"),
      limits = c(0.5, 1.0),
      na.value = "grey80",
      name = expression(pi[1])
    ) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(x = "Prenatal cell type (replication)", y = "Prenatal cell type (discovery)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}

pi1_int_heatmap <- plot_int_heatmap(pi1_int_tbl)
pi1_int_heatmap
```

### Jang pi1 enrichment {.tabset}

pi1 replication test (Storey & Tibshirani): what proportion of the tested
eQTL set shows non-null evidence in the comparison dataset, estimated from
the p-value distribution rather than a fixed significance threshold.

- Forward: pi1 of fetal-sig eQTL in Jang's nominal (full) data
- Reverse: pi1 of Jang-sig eQTL in fetal nominal data
- Forward and reverse are not symmetric: Jang (a 4-cohort meta-analysis) is
much better powered than any single fetal cell type, so forward pi1 tends
to run higher than reverse -- an asymmetric pair here reflects a power
difference between datasets, not necessarily a biological asymmetry

***

```{r pi1-jang-setup, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Shared by the Table and Heatmap subtabs (tabs render in document order)
pi1_fetal_l1 <- cell_types_L1
pi1_jang_l1  <- jang_l1

                                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

#### Heatmap {.tabset}

```{r pi1-jang-heatmap-prep, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
read_pi1_jang_results <- function(ct, jang_ct) {
  pi1_list <- read_rds(pick_file(jang_pi1_files, paste0(ct, "_vs_", jang_ct, "_")))
  tibble(
    cell_type = ct,
    jang_cell_type = jang_ct,
    pi1_forward = pi1_list$forward$pi1,
    pi1_reverse = pi1_list$reverse$pi1
  )
}

pi1_jang_tbl <- map2_dfr(pi1_combinations$cell_type, pi1_combinations$jang_cell_type,
                          read_pi1_jang_results)

pi1_jang_long <- pi1_jang_tbl |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(pi1_forward, pi1_reverse),
               names_to = "direction", values_to = "pi1") |>
  mutate(
    direction = recode(direction, pi1_forward = "Forward", pi1_reverse = "Reverse"),
    cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = pi1_fetal_l1),
    jang_cell_type = factor(jang_cell_type, levels = pi1_jang_l1)
  )

plot_pi1_jang_heatmap <- function(df) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = jang_cell_type, y = cell_type, fill = pi1)) +
    geom_tile(color = "black", lwd = 1.1, linetype = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(pi1), "NA", sprintf("%.2f", pi1))),
              color = "black", size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = c("white", "yellow", "red"),
      limits = c(0, 1.0),
      na.value = "grey80",
      name = expression(pi[1])
    ) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(x = "Cell type (Jang Ref)", y = "Cell type (Fetal Query)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}
```

### Effect-size concordance {.tabset}

Pearson correlation of eQTL betas between each fetal cell type and its
matched Jang et al. 2026 adult cell type. Points are highlighted only where
the pair is sig. in both datasets:

- Blue: sig. in both and concordant sign
- Red: sig. in both and discordant sign (also shown in opposite effects tab)
- Grey: sig. in fetal, not sig. in Jang

***

#### Significance counts

```{r beta-significance-counts, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
significance_counts |>
  select(Comparison = comparison,
         `Fetal-sig, present in adult` = n_fetal_sig_present_adult,
         `Also Jang-sig` = n_also_sig_jang,
         `Both-sig, concordant` = n_both_sig_concordant,
         `Both-sig, discordant` = n_both_sig_discordant) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Significance counts per fetal-adult comparison")
```

#### Scatter grid

```{r beta-scatter-grid, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=14, dpi=150}
plot_df <- paired_betas |>
  mutate(
    comparison = factor(paste(my_cell_type, "vs", jang_cell_type), levels = comparison_levels)
  ) |>
  # Plot "other" (grey) points first so blue/red highlighted points draw on top
  arrange(point_category == "other")

r_labels <- beta_cor_summary |>
  mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = comparison_levels),
         label = paste0("r = ", round(r, 3), "\nn = ", n))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = beta_my, y = beta_jang)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = point_category, alpha = point_category != "other", size = point_category != "other")) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "#377EB8", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = r_labels, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(concordant_both_sig = "#377EB8",
                                 discordant_both_sig = "#E41A1C",
                                 other = "grey70"),
                       labels = c(concordant_both_sig = "Concordant (sig. both)",
                                  discordant_both_sig = "Discordant (sig. both)",
                                  other = "Not sig. in both")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 0.7, `FALSE` = 0.25), guide = "none") +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1.1, `FALSE` = 0.6), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison, ncol = 4, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Fetal slope", y = "Adult (Jang) slope", colour = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

***

#### Opposite effects

- Sig. eQTL pairs in both fetal and Jang datasets with discordant effect
sign (the red points in the scatter grid).
- Fetal/Jang columns show `REF/ALT` for each dataset. No
AF column in Jang, so  `Allele_Status` is REF/ALT string comparison only.
Palindromic pairs (A/T, C/G) cannot be resolved so were excluded upstream (see repl_sc_beta_correlation.R).

```{r opposite-effects-table, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
opposite_effects |>
  mutate(
    Fetal = paste0(ref_my, "/", alt_my),
    Jang  = paste0(ref_jang, "/", alt_jang)
  ) |>
  select(Gene = external_gene_name, ENSG = gene, eSNP = snp,
         Fetal_Cell = my_cell_type, Jang_Cell = jang_cell_type,
         Beta_Fetal = beta_my, Beta_Jang = beta_jang,
         Fetal, Jang,
         Allele_Status = allele_status) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  small_dt()
```

***

### Benchmarking {.tabset}

***

#### Table

```{r benchmarking, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Benchmark files of the current runs are passed by the rule as rule=path pairs;
# files not yet written (rules not run) are skipped
benchmarks <- benchmark_files |>
  filter(file.exists(file)) |>
  pmap_dfr(function(rule, file) {
    df <- read.table(file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
    tibble(
      file = file,
      rule = rule,
      runtime_sec = df$s,
      runtime_hms = df$h.m.s.,
      max_rss = df$max_rss
    )
  })

# Summarise by rule
summary <- benchmarks |>
  group_by(rule) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_runtime_min = mean(runtime_sec) / 60,
    sd_runtime_min = sd(runtime_sec) / 60,
    mean_ram_gb = mean(max_rss) / 1024,
    sd_ram_gb = sd(max_rss) / 1024,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    sd_runtime_min = if_else(is.na(sd_runtime_min), 0, sd_runtime_min),
    sd_ram_gb = if_else(is.na(sd_ram_gb), 0, sd_ram_gb)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))) |>
  arrange(rule)

# Table
summary |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Benchmarking",
    subtitle = "Means and SD across replicates"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    rule = "Rule",
    n = "N",
    mean_runtime_min = "Mean Runtime (min)",
    sd_runtime_min = "SD Runtime (min)",
    mean_ram_gb = "Mean RAM (GB)",
    sd_ram_gb = "SD RAM (GB)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(mean_runtime_min, sd_runtime_min, mean_ram_gb, sd_ram_gb),
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(14),
    table.border.top.style = "none",
    table.border.bottom.style = "solid",
    table.border.bottom.width = px(2),
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    heading.align = "center"
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  )
```

***

#### Plot

***

```{r, runtime_plt, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.dim=c(10, 5)}
runtime_plt <- ggplot(summary, aes(x = reorder(rule, mean_runtime_min),
                                 y = mean_runtime_min)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(mean_runtime_min - ifelse(is.na(sd_runtime_min), 0, sd_runtime_min), 0),
                    ymax = mean_runtime_min + ifelse(is.na(sd_runtime_min), 0, sd_runtime_min)),
                width = 0.3, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Rule", y = "Runtime (minutes)",
       title = "Mean runtime per rule") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

mem_plt <- ggplot(summary, aes(x = reorder(rule, mean_ram_gb),
                                y = mean_ram_gb)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(mean_ram_gb - ifelse(is.na(sd_ram_gb), 0, sd_ram_gb), 0),
                    ymax = mean_ram_gb + ifelse(is.na(sd_ram_gb), 0, sd_ram_gb)),
                width = 0.3, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Rule", y = "RAM (GB)",
       title = "Mean RAM usage per rule") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

plot_grid(runtime_plt, mem_plt)
```
